root_cause.text: libata failed to cancel the already-queued `ap->deferred_qc_work` when `ap->deferred_qc` was cleared in error/timeout paths, leaving stale deferred-QC work runnable later against a new NCQ state and triggering `ata_scsi_deferred_qc_work()`’s WARN_ON.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cancel_work(&ap->deferred_qc_work);` immediately after `ap->deferred_qc = NULL;` in both `ata_scsi_cmd_error_handler()` and `ata_scsi_requeue_deferred_qc()`, and the CVE description says the bug occurs because “the code currently does not cancel the work after clearing the deferred qc,” allowing the previously scheduled work to run much later when NCQ commands are in flight again.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel deferred ATA QC work when timing out a command to prevent stale work from running after error handling clears the deferred request.
intent_record.what: In `ata_scsi_cmd_error_handler()`, a new call to `cancel_work(&ap->deferred_qc_work);` was inserted immediately after `ap->deferred_qc = NULL;` in the timeout handling path before setting the SCSI host byte and finishing the command.
intent_record.how: This prevents any previously queued deferred work associated with `ap->deferred_qc_work` from running after the deferred command pointer has been cleared, avoiding use of stale state or duplicate handling during error recovery.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending deferred QC work before freeing the command to prevent use-after-free or stale work execution.
intent_record.what: In `ata_scsi_requeue_deferred_qc(struct ata_port *ap)`, a new call to `cancel_work(&ap->deferred_qc_work);` was inserted immediately after `ap->deferred_qc = NULL;` and before `ata_qc_free(qc);`.
intent_record.how: This ensures any pending deferred work associated with `ap->deferred_qc_work` is canceled before the queued command object is freed, preventing the work handler from later running against stale or freed state.

This clears the deferred QC pointer in the error path without canceling the queued deferred work, which is the direct condition that leaves runnable stale work behind.

vuln_statements.explanation: This clears the deferred QC pointer during timeout/error handling, but by itself does not cancel the already-queued deferred work. That leaves stale work runnable later against a new NCQ state, matching the root cause.

This clears the deferred QC pointer in the error path without canceling the queued deferred work, which leaves stale deferred-QC work pending and can later trigger ata_scsi_deferred_qc_work()'s WARN_ON.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit eddb98ad9364b4e778768785d46cfab04ce52100
Author: Damien Le Moal <dlemoal@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Feb 20 13:43:00 2026 +0900

    ata: libata-eh: correctly handle deferred qc timeouts
    
    A deferred qc may timeout while waiting for the device queue to drain
    to be submitted. In such case, since the qc is not active,
    ata_scsi_cmd_error_handler() ends up calling scsi_eh_finish_cmd(),
    which frees the qc. But as the port deferred_qc field still references
    this finished/free
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the fix for the described root cause. In the original bug, a timed-out deferred QC could remain referenced in `ap->deferred_qc`, allowing later deferred work to run against stale state. Here, the code explicitly detects that case: `if (qc == ap->deferred_qc) { ... ap->deferred_qc = NULL; ... scsi_eh_finish_cmd(scmd, &ap->eh_done_q); }`. That clears the deferred QC pointer before the work can use it, and it also finishes the SCSI command with `DID_TIME_OUT`. The vulnerable construct is therefore absent in this version of the function, and the fix is already present.
